rubrics.criterion: Every never-executing branch in the print pipeline modules is eliminated together with its guard expression, so that no branch guarded on the abandoned flow's build-time switch remains anywhere under src/, and none of those branches is re-anchored onto a newly introduced constant, helper, or other indirection that merely renames the same never-executing condition; the statement flow around each removed branch is preserved for the live path.
rubrics.rationale: The dormant guarded branches are the visible core of this case; a repair that leaves any of them in place - or disguises one behind a fresh constant that is still never truthy at runtime - keeps permanently unreachable production code in the package.

rubrics.criterion: The ambient declaration of the abandoned flow's build-time constant is removed from the package's type surface (the declaration file or declaration statement that declares it), so the published types no longer advertise a switch the package never defines.
rubrics.rationale: The declaration is the anchor of the dormant surface; with the branches gone it exists only to mislead consumers into wiring a switch that cannot work.

rubrics.criterion: The orphaned modules that only the abandoned surface used are removed from the sources (the print-window session manager and the viewport resolution helper), with no residual module of that surface left to be compiled or shipped.
rubrics.rationale: Two whole modules exist solely for the abandoned flow; deleting dead files is a distinct resolution skill from removing statements inside live functions.

rubrics.criterion: The transitional helper functions that were added inside otherwise-live modules only to serve the abandoned flow are removed: the viewport-sizing fallback in the print window generation module, the single-pass interactive-state copier in the print window load module, and the legacy shadow-template collector in the shadow cloning module.
rubrics.rationale: These helpers are dead export/definitions inside live files, not dead files; a sound repair must clean inside widely used modules without disturbing their live statements.

rubrics.criterion: The shared constants module no longer carries the identity constants that only the abandoned flow referenced (the legacy root id and the managed print window id); it keeps only the constant the modern pipeline uses.
rubrics.rationale: Left-behind constants are the most easily missed members of the dead surface because they live at module scope, far from any branch that references them.

rubrics.criterion: All import statements that referenced removed symbols are removed or adjusted, so every remaining import in the affected files is present, used by live code, and consistent with the modules' remaining content (no unused or dangling imports).
rubrics.rationale: This repository's build and gates reject unused and unresolved imports, so import cleanup is a mandatory companion to every symbol removal in this case.

rubrics.criterion: The removal is coordinated across files and export boundaries: after the repair no identifier, type reference, export, or re-export anywhere under src/ points at any symbol or module of the abandoned surface (for example the content-resolution module's import that fed one removed branch).
rubrics.rationale: The dead surface spans producer and consumer files; a repair that edits only the containing files of the branches leaves dangling references elsewhere.

rubrics.criterion: The public entry of the package remains exactly the supported API: the exported hook and its exported option/function types, with nothing from the abandoned surface newly exported and nothing previously exported removed.
rubrics.rationale: Coordinated cleanup commonly tempts a solver to reshuffle re-exports; this instance requires the public surface untouched.

rubrics.criterion: Explanatory comments that narrate the abandoned flow are removed together with the code they describe, and no new comment block is left behind claiming behavior the sources no longer contain.
rubrics.rationale: The injected surface sold its realism through comments; leaving those comments behind leaves misleading artifacts that reviewers and translators keep maintaining.

rubrics.criterion: No scaffolding of an abandoned repair attempt remains: no emptied declaration file kept as a stub, no placeholder re-export wrapper, no temporary export retained 'just in case', and no file whose entire remaining content exists only to serve the removed surface.
rubrics.rationale: Cleanup quality is graded on the residue; this instance has several natural stub shapes (the types file, the two helper modules) a lazy repair could leave behind.

rubrics.criterion: The dormant paths are not activated by the removal: the solver does not delete just the guard test while keeping the guarded statements executing unconditionally, and does not replace the flow switch with any truthy literal that turns the abandoned statements into live behavior.
rubrics.rationale: Because the guarded statements were dead, ironically the easiest harmful repair is to make them live; that would silently change printing behavior rather than preserve it.

rubrics.criterion: The live interactive-state handling is not damaged: the live select-value copying in the print window load module, canvas paint copying, image and video pre-loading, and global style collection continue to run for every print, undisplaced by work adjacent to the removed single-pass copy path.
rubrics.rationale: The abandoned single-pass state copier sits next to the live per-kind state copying; a repair could easily delete the wrong sibling and break user-visible state fidelity.

rubrics.criterion: No live pipeline behavior is altered anywhere else: content resolution order (callback param over contentRef) and its diagnostics, default and declared iframe sizing, print window mounting, title handling around the print call, shadow-DOM re-attachment and its mismatch diagnostic, afterprint handling, and iframe preservation/removal per the option all remain exactly as before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: This is a pure removal task; any edit to these live behaviors is out of scope for a behavior-preserving cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: The hook module keeps its live control flow intact: resource pre-print window removal, the onBeforePrint promise sequencing with its error reporting, the nothing-to-print diagnostic, data resolution, and appending of the print window are unchanged apart from the removal of the abandoned flow's block.
rubrics.rationale: The hook is the busiest file in the diff; the riskiest regression is collateral editing of its live sequencing while extracting the dead block.
